data.name: Language
data.comment: The label of the language picker, read by screen readers.

data.name: NotFound
data.value: No such page. Go back to the {0}.
data.comment: {0} is a link to the overview page, with NavOverview as its text.

data.name: Days_Other
data.comment: A span of days, possibly with one decimal ("2.5 days").

data.name: JustNow
data.comment: How old a reading is, when the source's clock is ahead of ours.

data.name: UnderAMinute
data.comment: How old a reading is.

data.name: Percent
data.comment: A percentage; {0} is the number. Some languages put a space before the sign.

data.name: ModeSolarSummary
data.value: Charges from the sun the house isn't using, once the home battery is full.

data.name: ModeForecastedSummary
data.value: Charges from surplus like Solar, but the forecast decides how much of today's sun the car may have, so the home battery still reaches 100% by the evening.

data.name: ModeSolarGridSummary
data.value: Follows the sun, and lets the grid top the charger up to its minimum when the surplus alone is too small.

data.name: ModeFastSummary
data.value: Charges as fast as the installation allows, from the sun and the grid, with the home battery kept out of it.

data.name: ModeTargetedSummary
data.value: Delivers a set amount by a set time: forecast surplus first, the rest bought from the grid as late as it can.

data.name: ModeChange
data.comment: A session that started in one charge mode and ended in another.

data.name: WeatherLine
data.comment: {0} is a temperature, {1} a percentage of sky covered by cloud.

data.name: WeatherLineWithCondition
data.comment: {0} is the weather provider's own description (not translated), {1} a temperature, {2} the cloud percentage.

data.name: DayForecastLine
data.comment: A day's expected solar energy, with its pessimistic (p10) and optimistic (p90) bounds.

data.name: AboutTopic
data.comment: The accessible name of an (i) button that explains a figure; {0} is the figure's label.

data.name: SignInOnCarPage
data.value: Sign in on the car page

data.name: RestartProgress
data.value: Restarting… The charger is being paused and the open session closed. This page reloads by itself once the controller is back.

data.name: RestartNotBack
data.value: If it does not come back within a minute or two, nothing is restarting it: see {0} or {1}, or start it again by hand.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are shell commands, shown as code.

data.name: RestartCost
data.value: A charge in progress is paused, and the controller comes back in Off, as it does after any start — the charging mode, a Targeted request and a Fast limit are not kept, so choose them again afterwards. This UI and Home Assistant are unreachable for roughly half a minute. Starting up fetches the solar forecast, so a restart spends one of the day's Solcast calls when a key is configured. It comes back by itself under Docker's {0} and the .deb's systemd unit; run any other way — {1}, a plain {2}, the Windows zip — it simply exits and has to be started again.
data.comment: {0}, {1} and {2} are configuration and commands, shown as code.

data.name: MqttBrokerNote
data.value: — what the controller dials, which is not necessarily reachable from here.

data.name: MqttPasswordWithheld
data.value: set, and not shown here — this UI has no login, so anyone on the network could read it. Configure {0} ({1}) to make it readable.
data.comment: {0} is an environment variable and {1} a command, shown as code.

data.name: SignInTitle
data.comment: The browser tab of the sign-in page.

data.name: SignInHint
data.value: One password for this installation, chosen on its Setup page the first time it ran or set as {0}. There is no reset from here: a forgotten one is replaced in the settings on the machine itself.
data.comment: {0} is an environment variable, shown as code.

data.name: SetupTitle
data.comment: The browser tab of the setup page.

data.name: AlreadySetUpText
data.value: This installation already has a password. {0}.
data.comment: {0} is a link whose text is SignIn.

data.name: SetupIntro
data.value: Gleanvolt can show this installation's energy and charging history, and change how the charger is driven. It is reachable by anything on this network, so it needs a password before it will show any of that.

data.name: SetupNote
data.value: One password for this installation, not an account per person. Keep it somewhere you can find it: there is no reset from inside the UI, only editing the settings file on the machine itself.

data.name: PasswordsDiffer
data.value: The two passwords are not the same.

data.name: PasswordNotSaved
data.value: The password could not be saved on this installation, so it has not been set. Set Web__PasswordHash in the configuration instead.
